issues.problem: The how line said it is not used for shared tastes, but it is commonly used for people with shared interests (book clubs, hobby sites), which contradicts ctx 3 and ctx 5

issues.problem: bad 1 (liking spicy food, 真是志同道合) reads as playful hyperbole, so a native speaker would not find it clearly wrong
issues.action: Replaced it with a grammar misuse: the idiom used as a verb with an object (志同道合了几个新朋友)

issues.problem: ctx 1, 3 and 6 showed only ingratitude, so 忘恩负义 fits them just as well
issues.action: Rewrote all three so the benefactor is actively harmed (cheated, reported, killed)

issues.problem: ctx 4 (old man in front of his old house) fits 泪流满面 (cy228, same set) just as well
issues.action: Rewrote it so he holds the tears back, which only fits tears welling in the eyes

issues.problem: ctx 4 (accountant checking the director's receipts) and ctx 2 (a judge who favours no one) are stern impartiality, so 铁面无私 fits as well or better
issues.action: Rewrote both around putting the common good above one's own interest (giving up a flat to a needier colleague; not pocketing funds)
